main_issue: Whether the housewarming at the shared flat will be alcohol-free (given D's sobriety) despite A's bought drinks and B's manager expecting drinks.

A-B.evidence: B initially praised A's purchase and approved the storage plan (T10), but at T17 rejected the dry-party plan A accepted (T16); at T29 A says 'We already agreed... B, you just have to tell him.'

A-C.evidence: C backed A's storage plan (T12) and later pushed for an alcohol-free party (T18), matching A's acceptance at T16 and insistence at T29.

A-D.evidence: D rejected A's storage plan (T13); A accepted D's proposal to redirect the money to food and non-alcoholic drinks (T16), and both say the party is alcohol-free (T28, T29).

B-C.evidence: C backed the storage plan (T12) with B, but at T18 C suggested B tell the manager it's dry, and B rejected that (T19); C's drink-first idea at T20 was also rejected (T22).

B-D.evidence: D offered B several workarounds (T21, T23) and B rejected them (T22); D then says 'the party will be alcohol-free, up to you how to handle it' (T28), while B keeps objecting (T27).

C-D.evidence: D pushed for a fully alcohol-free party (T13); C then argued for telling the manager it's dry (T18) and D endorsed C's drink idea (T21).
